chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Isma'il ibn Muhammad from his grandfather Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

That wishing (for death) is the work of whispering (of Satan), and the greatest snare of Satan is eating clay. Indeed, eating clay causes illness in the body and stirs up the disease. And whoever eats clay and becomes weaker than his strength that was before he ate it, he becomes weaker than the work he used to do before he ate it; he will be accounted for what is between his weakness and his strength, and punished for it.

key_terms.التَّمَنِّي: Wishing (specifically for death or the end of life)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical significance of eating clay according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) connects the spiritual malady of 'wishing' (tamannī) with the physical act of eating clay, presenting the latter as a tangible snare of Satan that induces bodily weakness. This physical decline directly impacts spiritual capacity, meaning those who consume clay and lose their strength are held accountable for the good deeds they could have performed had they remained strong, illustrating the Shia principle of the interdependence of physical health and spiritual productivity.
